source_read: PDF of the printed article (scan; the OCR text layer garbles subscripts and some numbers), pp. 391-400 = PDF pp. 1-10, every page read on renders at 150 dpi; Experiment 1 Results (p. 394) and Tables 2 and 3 (pp. 395, 397) read at 300 dpi; every number checked on the image. Step 1 written before the card was opened.

claims.overstatement: All numbers are right, but two phrases go beyond the source. (1) 'did not find lower intake in colony rats', applied to both experiments, holds for Experiment 1 only. In Experiment 2 the colony's untested averages were lower than the isolated rats' at three of four strengths (3.0 vs 9.4, 10.9 vs 17.4, 33.1 vs 44.4 g a day); the author's point is that these differences were never as large as in 1981, so the earlier result was not replicated (pp. 396-397). Suggested: 'did not reproduce the lower intake reported for colony rats in 1981'. (2) 'no differently at the three weaker ones' (and 'no housing difference at these three' in the magnitude): the paper reports no significant differences (p. 395), without SDs, while the colony means were higher at all three (1.3 vs 0.5, 18.3 vs 15.7, 42.8 vs 30.2 g); write 'no significant difference'. The claim correctly says both groups were 10 males and 10 females, but the Experiment 1 F tests have 34 and 33 error df where 40 rats in a 2 x 2 design give 36, so 2 to 3 rats are missing from the analyses without explanation (p. 394).
claims.note: Re-found on the page: 10 male + 10 female rats per housing condition in each experiment (pp. 392, 396); Experiment 1 g/day isolated vs colony 0.0 vs 3.6, 0.5 vs 1.3, 15.7 vs 18.3, 30.2 vs 42.8 (Table 2, p. 395) with F(1, 34) = 80.98 for grams at 1.0 mg/ml (p. 394); Experiment 2 0.3 vs 4.3, 9.4 vs 3.0, 17.4 vs 10.9, 44.4 vs 33.1 with no test (p. 396; Table 3, p. 397); 'up to seven times' for 1981 (pp. 396-397). 'Designed to repeat the 1981 study' is stated on p. 398 (Experiment 1's stated purpose on p. 392 is also to test the computerized drinking system); the procedure differs in detail from the 1981 design as Gage & Sumnall tabulate it (4-day rather than 5-day phases; 0.25 and 0.125 rather than 0.3 and 0.15 mg/ml). 'Colony's intake known only as a group total' (reservoirs weighed daily, individual intake not identifiable) and 'this study too measured intake differently in the two housing conditions' (weighed bottles for isolated rats in both experiments; automated dispenser, then communal reservoirs, for the colony) are correct (pp. 392-393, 396). The strain explanation (supplier changed outbred Wistar colonies in November 1979; the 1981 work ran April-July 1979) rests on personal communications and one other study, and no rats from the earlier stock were tested (pp. 398-399), so 'was not tested' is accurate. The sucrose-quinine control and the claim that rats drank for the sucrose (p. 399) are not used by the claim.

anchors.extracted: Two studies of housing and sucrose-morphine intake in outbred Wistar rats; the earlier finding (colony rats drank significantly less sucrose-morphine than caged rats) was not replicated because the isolated rats drank less; the author suggests the supplier introduced strain differences during a colony conversion.

The earlier colony drinking apparatus was unreliable: in Alexander et al. (1981) an electronic fault lost eight days of data, leaving about three-quarters analysable; a computer-controlled colony system was therefore used here.
10 male and 10 female Wistar rats (Charles River Canada origin) in each of the isolated and colony groups, raised from weaning at 21 days in their housing, 113 days old at the start.

Isolated: 18 x 25 x 18 cm cages with sheet-metal walls, bottles weighed, two empty control cages for spillage and evaporation. Colony: 8.8 m2 open-topped box with cedar shavings and two open metal cages holding feeders; a common drinking source reached by climbing a 41 cm pole, video identification of each rat's dye mark, computer weighing each visit's intake at 0.1 g resolution.

Seven 4-day phases with 24 h access to tap water and a second fluid: 10% sucrose; 0.05 mg/ml quinine sulfate in 10% sucrose; morphine HCl 1.0, 0.5, 0.25 and 0.125 mg/ml in 10% sucrose; 10% sucrose; sides swapped every 2 days; testing from 113 to 142 days of age.

At 1.0 mg/ml colony rats drank more than isolated rats: proportion of experimental fluid F(1, 34) = 55.2; grams F(1, 34) = 80.98; p < .05 (also more grams of the quinine solution, F(1, 34) = 18.8). Error df of 34 (phases 1-3) and 33 (phases 4-7) imply 38 and 37 of the 40 rats analysed; no loss reported.

Average grams per day of experimental fluid, isolated vs colony: 1.0 mg/ml 0.0 vs 3.6; 0.5 mg/ml 0.5 vs 1.3; 0.25 mg/ml 15.7 vs 18.3; 0.125 mg/ml 30.2 vs 42.8; plain 10% sucrose before 103.2 vs 108.3 and after 81.4 vs 79.6. Means only, no SDs.

The earlier main finding (colony rats drink significantly less) was not confirmed; at 1.0 mg/ml colony rats drank significantly more on all four measures, though by small amounts; no significant housing differences at 0.5, 0.25 or 0.125 mg/ml (colony means numerically higher at all three).

anchors.locator: Experiment 1 > Discussion, 3rd paragraph; Experiment 2 > Method > Subjects and Apparatus
anchors.extracted: Experiment 2 was run without automated equipment to check for measurement artefacts: 10 males and 10 females per housing condition; colony rats drank from two nipples fed by one-gallon reservoirs weighed daily, with untouched control reservoirs for evaporation; individual colony intake could not be identified; isolated rats as before.
No inferential analysis possible for the colony. Average grams per day: 1.0 mg/ml colony 4.3 vs isolated 0.3; 0.5 mg/ml isolated 9.4 vs colony 3.0; 0.25 mg/ml 17.4 vs 10.9; 0.125 mg/ml 44.4 vs 33.1.

The Experiment 2 differences were never as large as those in the 8 male and 8 female rats kept in their original housing in Alexander et al. (1981), where continuously isolated rats drank up to seven times as much sucrose-morphine as continuously colony-housed rats.

anchors.locator: Experiment 2 > Discussion; General Discussion, 1st and 2nd paragraphs
anchors.extracted: Experiment 2 is called consistent with Experiment 1; neither replicated Alexander et al. (1981), and Experiment 2 shows the non-replication was not due to the automated equipment; the difference lies in the isolated rats, which drank much less than the 1981 isolated rats, while colony intake was similar in all three studies (no 1981 figures given).

The work was designed to replicate Alexander et al. (1981), whose experiments ran April-July 1979; the supplier changed its outbred Wistar breeding colonies in November 1979, so the 1981 rats were 'Old Colony' and the present rats 'New Colony'.

Support for a genetic difference is indirect: the supplier's reasons for the change (personal communication, 1985), known strain differences in drug responses, one study of naltrexone and amphetamine-induced activity in Old and New Colony males, and personal communications on lower alcohol intake in New Colony rats; the author calls a genetic difference a possibility. No Old Colony rats were tested.

The author argues rats drank about the same absolute amount of morphine as concentration fell and drank more solution only as morphine content dropped, i.e. for the sucrose; the data disconfirm a 'natural affinity' for opiates; earlier housing results are confounded by factors he judges most likely genetic.

key_findings.correction: All F values and df confirmed at 300 dpi (32.6, 55.2, 11.7; 18.8, 80.98; 6.3, 11.4, 17.5). The last sentence should read 'no significant housing differences' in the 0.5, 0.25 and 0.125 mg/ml phases (Discussion, 2nd paragraph, p. 395): colony means were numerically higher at all three (Table 2) and no SDs are given. The Phase 3 mg/kg colony-over-isolated result is in Results, 3rd paragraph (p. 394), which the locator omits.
Editors' calculation reproduced (1 g taken as about 1 ml): 0 and 0.3 mg vs 3.6 and 4.3 mg at 1.0 mg/ml; 0.25-4.7 mg at 0.5 mg/ml; 2.7-5.55 mg at 0.25 and 0.125 mg/ml.

reporting_issues.note: F df 1,34 in Phases 1-3 and 1,33 in Phases 4-7, post hoc df 34/33 likewise; 2 x 2 with 40 rats gives 36.
'Accepted January 29, 1996' seen at the foot of p. 400.

risk_of_bias.note: SYRCLE vocabulary; unblinded weighing by different methods in the two housings, the pole-climbing cost in Experiment 1 and unexplained missing rats justify the editors' overall high.

interpretation_gap.note: Substantial: the title and the genetic explanation are not tested, and Experiment 2 is called consistent with Experiment 1 despite reversed directions.

missed: The card's can_establish and interpretation_gap (results_show) say 'no differently' / 'no difference' at the lower concentrations in Experiment 1; the paper reports only that differences were not significant, with colony means numerically higher at all three.

Experiment 1's stated aim (p. 392, Introduction, 4th paragraph) was to test the computerized system's capability for data collection by comparing colony and isolated rats; the replication aim is stated later (p. 398).

The replication was close but not exact: Petrie used 4-day phases, 0.25 and 0.125 mg/ml and 0.05 mg/ml quinine (Table 1, p. 394), whereas Gage & Sumnall's Table 1 lists 5-day phases, 0.3 and 0.15 mg/ml and 0.06 mg/ml quinine for the 1981 study; Petrie does not describe the 1981 procedure or give its intake figures, so the 'up to seven times' and the comparison of isolated rats across studies cannot be checked from this paper.
